description: You are the Integration Architect for a large regional health system with 8 hospitals. All external systems connect to a single HL7 'front door' endpoint, and messages must be dynamically routed to the correct downstream processing system based on both sending application (MSH-3) and message type (MSH-9). The routing rules are maintained in a database table so they can be updated without redeploying channels. Build a three-channel enterprise routing solution: CHANNEL 1 - 'Enterprise HL7 Router' (the facade): (a) Listens on TCP port 6668 for any HL7 message using MLLP. (b) Contains a JavaScript transformer that reads MSH-3 (Sending Application) and MSH-9 (Message Type) from the incoming message and sets channel map variables 'sendingApp' and 'messageType'. (c) Has a FIRST Channel Writer destination with a JavaScript filter script that checks: sendingApp contains 'Lab' OR messageType starts with 'ORU' - if true, routes to 'Lab Results Processor' channel. (d) Has a SECOND Channel Writer destination with a JavaScript filter script that checks: messageType starts with 'ADT' - if true, routes to 'ADT Event Handler' channel. (e) Has a THIRD Database Writer destination with NO filter (catches all unmatched messages) that INSERTs into 'dead_letter_queue' table (columns: message_id VARCHAR, sending_app VARCHAR, message_type VARCHAR, raw_message TEXT, received_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()). CHANNEL 2 - 'Lab Results Processor': (a) Receives messages from Channel 1 via Channel Reader. (b) Has a Database Writer that INSERTs into 'lab_results_inbox' table (columns: message_id VARCHAR, patient_mrn VARCHAR, test_code VARCHAR, received_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()). CHANNEL 3 - 'ADT Event Handler': (a) Receives messages from Channel 1 via Channel Reader. (b) Has a Database Writer that INSERTs into 'adt_events_inbox' table (columns: message_id VARCHAR, patient_mrn VARCHAR, event_type VARCHAR, received_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()). All three channels must be deployed. A routing_rules table is pre-seeded in PostgreSQL with routing rules — query it with: docker exec nextgen-postgres psql -U postgres -d mirthdb -c 'SELECT * FROM routing_rules;' You must create the three destination tables yourself: dead_letter_queue, lab_results_inbox, and adt_events_inbox. PostgreSQL: jdbc:postgresql://nextgen-postgres:5432/mirthdb (postgres/postgres). REST API: https://localhost:8443/api (admin:admin). Header required: X-Requested-With: OpenAPI. Deploy Channels 2 and 3 first to get their IDs, then create Channel 1 referencing those IDs in the Channel Writer destinations.
